title: NHRC, India takessuo motucognizance of reported burn injuries to a woman after people allegedly poured boiling water on her, branding her a witch in Bhojpur village, Garhwa district, Jharkhand
subtitle:
​​​​​​​
Issues notices to the Garhwa District Magistrate and SP, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks
The report to include the status of the victim’s health and compensation, if any, paid to her
body_text:
The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India has taken suo motu cognizance of a media report that a woman suffered 40% burn injuries after being attacked by a group of people, branding her a witch in Bhojpur village, Garhwa district, Jharkhand. Reportedly, the perpetrators, who are residing in the same village, poured boiling water on the victim during the attack.
The Commission has observed that the contents of the news, if true, raise serious issues of violation of human rights. Therefore, it has issued notices to the Garhwa District Magistrate and Superintendent of Police, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks. It is expected to include the status of the victim’s health and compensation, if any, paid to her.
According to the media report, carried on 24th August 2026, the victim was admitted to the hospital for medical treatment and an investigation is underway.
***
NSK

enrichment.summary: The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) has taken suo motu cognizance of a media report that a woman suffered 40% burn injuries after villagers in Bhojpur, Garhwa district, Jharkhand, poured boiling water on her after branding her a witch. NHRC has issued notices to the Garhwa District Magistrate and Superintendent of Police seeking a detailed report within two weeks, including the victim's health status and any compensation paid. The victim is currently hospitalised and an investigation is underway.
enrichment.context: Witch-hunting remains a persistent social problem in parts of rural India, particularly in states like Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Assam and Bihar, often linked to superstition, land disputes, or targeting of vulnerable women (especially widows or those without male family support). Jharkhand has a specific law, the Prevention of Witch (DAAIN) Practices Act, 2001, to address such violence, though enforcement remains weak. The NHRC frequently exercises its suo motu powers under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 to intervene in such cases by directing state authorities to investigate, ensure medical treatment, and provide compensation to victims, functioning as a check on custodial and non-custodial human rights violations. This particular release reflects a routine, case-specific intervention rather than a broader policy or systemic reform announcement.
